title: Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Joint Receive Beamforming and Power Allocation for Distributed Maritime Sensing Networks Under Limited Samples and Backhaul Constraints
content: Distributed maritime sensing requires receive-beamforming and power-allocation decisions based on short interference-training records and subject to limited cooperative-link capacity. We formulate a design that maximizes the worst-node signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) with a squared 2-Wasserstein ambiguity set and a radius explicitly selected using an engineering rule. A homogeneous worst-case quadratic form yields a complete second-order cone programming (SOCP) formulation at a fixed SINR threshold. A loaded receive update is distinguished from this exact block, and both are followed by power allocation using the complete robust denominator. A power iteration with upward quantization and a mean-preserving quantized tracker provide hard-budget feasibility checks on a reliable shared broadcast channel. We derive coupled error bounds and a conditional bound on the gap to a centralized power optimum computed using the same data and fixed receive weights; joint stationarity is not established. In 200 paired simulations with known ensemble clutter covariance and a spatial jamming surrogate, certified loading achieves mean worst-node SINRs of 2.663 and 1.928 dB when evaluated using the true covariance and the robust denominator, respectively. Both certified loading and the exact-receive branch have zero observed robust violations, whereas the reduced-denominator diagnostic violates the complete constraint in every trial. A 256-bit round cap is enforced before sending, and small per-round messages do not imply lower traffic over a complete coherent processing interval (CPI): certified loading uses a mean of 20.799 kbit over the 200 core scenes, compared with 20.802 kbit for a matched centralized implementation with one binary64 Hermitian covariance upload, the same three redesign rounds, and a final return. This matched comparison demonstrates no complete-CPI traffic advantage. Independent detector counts, paired confidence intervals, solver statuses, and per-trial feasibility records are released.
